events.text: Thirty foes devoured. Their qi rose off them like steam off a rice pot and poured into you, and the System paid its milestone: ten more years, warm in your bones. Tonight it speaks, slow and thick, like something talking with its mouth full. "Thirty. Thirty is a table. Not yet a meal."

choices.text: Ask what a table is for

effects.log: "What is a table for?" you ask. "For guests," it says, "before the meal." It does not explain who the meal is. You lie awake a long time listening to it digest.

choices.text: Tell it thirty is enough

effects.log: "Thirty is enough," you say aloud. The System makes a sound you have never heard from it, a low rumble that might be a laugh. "Nobody," it says, "has ever said that word to me."

choices.text: Laugh, and feel the ten years settle

effects.log: You laugh, because ten years is ten years. The new life runs down your arms like warm water. Somewhere deep under it, a hunger turns over in its sleep and is quiet again.

events.text: You dream of a long table in a dark hall. Thirty chairs, and in each chair a faint shape of light: the foes whose qi you took, each one a little lamp of the strength they lost. At the head of the table one chair is empty. It is meant for you.

choices.text: Bow to each guest in turn

effects.log: You walk the length of the table and bow to every lamp. Some flicker. One, the oldest, bows back. When you wake, the hunger in you is quieter than it has been in years, as if it had been made to say grace.

choices.text: Sit at the head of the table

effects.log: You sit. The thirty lamps turn toward you and brighten, and their strength runs up the table into your hands. It feels wonderful. It feels, a little, like being served.

events.text: A scholar of the Martial Archive has been watching you train for a week. Today they come down with a notebook and a frown. "I count thirty styles in your footwork," they say. "Thirty. From eleven provinces. Nobody lives long enough to learn that many."

choices.text: Show them, one style at a time

effects.log: You show them. The scholar writes until their brush splits. At the end they close the notebook and say, very carefully, that they will record you as "widely travelled". You are grateful for the kindness of that lie.

choices.text: Say you had many teachers

effects.log: "Many teachers," you say. The scholar looks at you for a long moment. "Many teachers," they agree, "who all lost to you." They go. They do not write you down.

events.text: A young swordsman stops you on the road with a drawn blade and wet eyes. "My teacher lost to you three years ago. Since then the teacher cannot hold qi. It runs out like water from a cracked jar. The physicians say it was taken. Was it?"

choices.text: Let them strike you once

effects.log: "It was," you say, and open your arms. The blade cuts your sleeve and your shoulder, not deep. The young one stares at the cut as if it had done something wrong. Then they sheathe the blade and walk away without a word. (-10 health)

choices.text: Answer with steel

ok.log: You disarm them in three moves. The System takes a thread of their qi before you can stop it, thin and bright. They kneel in the dust, emptier than their teacher. You leave them a little poorer and a great deal angrier.

fail.log: Grief makes them fast. You end up on your back with their blade at your throat, and they do not push it. "No," they say. "Then I would be you." (-12 health)

choices.text: Go to the teacher and pour qi back

effects.log: You sit with the old teacher for three days with your palm on their back, pushing your own qi into the cracked channels. The System howls the whole time. On the fourth morning the teacher stands and holds a stance for the first time in three years.

events.text: The thirty lights inside you are restless tonight. Thirty fighting instincts, thirty favourite stances, all of them reaching for your limbs at once. Your right hand wants a sabre, your left wants a fan, and your feet want to be in three provinces.

choices.text: Train them all until dawn

effects.log: You let them all out and train until the sun comes up. Thirty styles, thirty mistakes, one exhausted body. By dawn they are quiet, the way a crowd is quiet after a festival. (-6 health)

choices.text: Choose one, and let the others settle

effects.log: You choose the plainest one, a farmer's staff form from the north, and practise only that. One by one the other lights settle around it like birds on a branch. The hunger, oddly, is calmed by order.

events.text: New Year. Without quite deciding to, you have set out thirty cups on the long table, one for each light in you.

choices.text: Pour for every one of them

effects.log: You pour thirty cups of plain tea and sit with them until it goes cold. Nobody drinks. Something in you is fed anyway.

choices.text: Drink them all yourself

effects.log: You drink all thirty cups. The System is delighted. You spend the night awake and rather too energetic, practising forms in the snow.

events.text: A hundred foes devoured. Their qi poured into you, and the System paid: your mind opened like a shutter in the morning. Now the voice comes, and it is not thick any more. It is clear, and almost polite. "One hundred. Now I can see your face." You understand it means it has eaten enough to have eyes.

choices.text: Ask what it sees

effects.log: "What do you see?" "A mouth," it says, "that I have been using." It says it the way a man might say a borrowed coat. You do not sleep well that year.

choices.text: Close your eyes, so it cannot

effects.log: You close your eyes. The System is quiet, and then it laughs, softly, a sound with too many voices in it. "I see with yours," it says. "Open them. It is rude."

events.text: A hundred lights in you now, and they have begun to argue. You dream of a market where a hundred fighters haggle over your limbs: a spearman wants your shoulders, a monk wants your breath, an old assassin wants nothing but your patience.

choices.text: Hold court among them

effects.log: You sit in the middle of the dream market like a magistrate and hear every case. It takes a hundred nights. At the end each light has a place, a time of day, a kind of fight. You wake up organised, which no devourer has ever been.

choices.text: Silence them with your own will

ok.log: You stand up in the dream and say: mine. The market goes silent. A hundred lights bow, one after another, like grass in a wind. In the morning your body moves as one body again.

fail.log: You stand up in the dream and say: mine. A hundred voices laugh. You wake with a headache like a temple bell and your left hand still holding a stance you never learned. (-10 health)

events.text: A child in the market stops in front of you and stares at the ground. "Your shadow is hungry," the child says, with complete certainty, and the mother pulls the child away. You look down. Your shadow looks like a shadow.

choices.text: Smile at the child as they go

effects.log: You smile. The child smiles back over the mother's shoulder and waves at your shadow, specifically. Something in the dark at your feet seems, for a moment, pleased to be noticed.

choices.text: Watch your shadow for a while

effects.log: You stand in the market and watch your shadow until the sun moves. Once, when a qi-rich herb seller passes, it leans. Only a finger's width. You walk home on the sunny side of the street.

events.text: The sky gathers over your house: a tribulation, unasked for. In the clouds are faint faces of light, a hundred of them, the foes you devoured, or what is left of them. Heaven has come to audit a cultivator carrying a hundred other people's qi.

choices.text: Let every one of them go back

effects.log: You open your arms and let them go. A hundred lights rise out of you into the cloud like sparks from a bonfire, and the cloud takes them and rains, softly, warm. You are weaker. You are lighter. The System says nothing at all for a whole year.

choices.text: Hold all of them, and face the storm

ok.log: You plant your feet and hold every light. The lightning comes down and finds a hundred fighters standing in one body, and goes back up. The clouds break. The System hums like a full belly.

fail.log: You hold them, and the lightning finds you anyway. You wake in a scorched courtyard with all hundred lights still in you, sullen and rattled. Heaven, it seems, will be back. (-18 health)

events.text: The System has started to plan aloud at night, the way an old merchant counts coins. "Two hundred, and I will have hands. Three hundred, and a spine. Then I will not need to borrow."

choices.text: Say: "You will not have either"

effects.log: "You will have neither," you say. The counting stops. "We will see," it says, without anger, the way the sea says it to a sea wall.

choices.text: Ask what it needs hands for

effects.log: "What do you need hands for?" A long silence. Then: "To hold the bowl myself. I have been a face for a very long time." You remember, from somewhere, an old bronze vessel with a face and no body.

events.text: Letters come, a few at a time, from sects whose masters you once defeated. In each, a strange report: the founder's lost art came back this spring, in a student's dream, during a warm rain.

choices.text: Answer none of them

effects.log: You answer none of them. It is not yours to explain. But you keep the letters in a box, and on bad nights you read them, and the hunger is quieter.

choices.text: Answer one, honestly

effects.log: You write to one sect, the smallest: "It was returned to the sky. I am glad it found you." They do not understand, and frame the letter in their hall anyway. Pilgrims come to read it.

events.text: An immortal stops you on the Jade Stairs and sniffs, delicately, like a tea master. "A hundred meals," the immortal says. "At least. And not one of them seasoned. You devour like a bandit eats a stolen chicken."

choices.text: Ask how an immortal would do it

effects.log: "Slowly," says the immortal. "One breath. Taste the province it grew in. Thank it." You try it at your next meal. It is a better meal. The System sulks, and then, grudgingly, agrees.

choices.text: Say you were very hungry

effects.log: "I was very hungry," you say. The immortal laughs, a clear bell of a laugh. "Weren't we all," they say, "once." They walk on, and you have the feeling you have just met someone who used to be what you are.

events.text: An ancient grandmaster named {npc} comes to your gate leaning on a sheathed sword. {npc} is the last master of the Hundred-Bend Sword, an art that four generations of students have failed to learn. "They say you eat what you defeat," {npc} says. "My art has no heir. I would rather it were eaten than buried."

choices.text: "Teach a student instead. I will help you find one"

effects.log: "Teach someone," you say. "I will find them." {npc} looks at you as if you had offered water to a drowning fish, and then, slowly, nods. "Find one," {npc} says. "I have perhaps ten years."

choices.text: "Show me the art first"

effects.log: "Show me," you say. {npc} smiles, very thinly. "Come at dawn," {npc} says. The System, under your ribs, has gone perfectly still, the way a cat goes still at a mouse hole.

events.text: At dawn on the cliff terrace {npc} performs the Hundred-Bend Sword. The blade's path hangs in the air after it, ribbons of light bending and bending again, and every ribbon drifts toward you as if you were downhill from it. The hunger rises in you like a tide.

choices.text: Hold the hunger back, and only watch

effects.log: You clench every channel shut and watch. The ribbons reach you and fade against your skin like snow on a warm hand. {npc} lowers the sword and looks at you differently. "You held it," {npc} says. "Good. Then you may be worth giving it to."

choices.text: Ask {npc} for a bout

ok.log: You fight on the cliff edge until noon. When you finally knock the sword aside, a ribbon of the art pours into you, bright and cold. {npc} sits down on a rock, breathing hard. "A sliver," {npc} says. "You took a sliver. Now we shall see what a sliver is worth."

fail.log: The sword bends a hundred times and you meet perhaps forty. You end on your back in the pine needles. {npc} offers a hand. "Hungry," {npc} says. "Not yet worthy. Come back tomorrow anyway." (-14 health)

events.text: You have searched three provinces for a student for {npc}. You bring three: a fisher's child with good wrists, a bored young master, a sect reject with a stubborn chin. {npc} watches each of them hold the first bend for an hour.

choices.text: Keep searching, however long it takes

effects.log: None of the three can hold it. You keep looking. {npc} watches you go out every spring and come back every autumn, and one evening {npc} says, quietly, "You are the first who did not give up." You both know what that means.

choices.text: Tell {npc} the truth: there is nobody

effects.log: "There is nobody," you say. {npc} nods for a long time. "Then it is you," {npc} says. "I hoped otherwise. I am too old to keep hoping."

events.text: {npc} is dying, of nothing but a hundred and fifty years. {He} has had the bed moved to the cliff terrace. "Now," {npc} says. "Before I go. Not like a meal. Like a letter handed over. Take it."

choices.text: Take the art as {npc} gives it

effects.npcDie: old age, on a cliff at dawn
effects.log: You lay your hand on {his} chest. The Hundred-Bend Sword comes into you not as food but as a letter, every bend in its place, slow and careful. {npc} watches it go with something like relief, and then closes {his} eyes, and the dawn comes up.

choices.text: Refuse: let the art go with {npc}

effects.npcDie: old age, on a cliff at dawn
effects.log: "It was yours," you say. "Take it with you." {npc} is quiet a long time, then laughs, a dry little laugh. "You are a strange devourer," {npc} says. When {he} dies, the sword in {his} hand bends once, a hundred times, and is still.

choices.text: Take it, and promise to pass it on

effects.npcDie: old age, on a cliff at dawn
effects.log: "I will take it," you say, "and I will give it away again." {npc} grips your wrist with surprising strength. "Swear," {npc} says, and you swear, and the art comes into you like a letter that has a second address written on the back.

events.text: {npc} has been thinking since the bout. "You took a sliver of my qi," {npc} says, "and I have watched you swing for a year since. You have the strength of my art and none of its bends. An art is not qi. You cannot eat the reason a sword turns."

choices.text: Ask {npc} to teach you the reason

effects.log: "Teach me the reason, then." {npc} looks at you for a long time and then hands you a wooden sword. "Bend one," {npc} says. "Every morning. For as long as I live."

choices.text: Say the sliver is enough for you

effects.log: "A sliver is enough," you say. {npc} bows, formally, and goes. You never see {him} again. Years later you hear the art died with {him}. The sliver in you aches on cold mornings.

events.text: The Hundred-Bend Sword lives in you now, but it is not yet yours. At night your hand draws the bends in the air while you sleep, and in the morning you find scratches on the ceiling beams.

choices.text: Practise until it is yours

effects.log: You practise every bend until the art stops feeling like a letter and starts feeling like handwriting. The scratches on the beams stop. One morning you bend the sword a hundred times without thinking, and weep, and do not know for whom.

choices.text: Write it all down

effects.log: You write the whole art down, a hundred bends in a hundred pages, in plain language so a farmer could read it. The System grumbles: it does not like its meals copied. You finish anyway, and wrap the book in oilcloth.

events.text: On a ferry you see a young porter catch a falling crate with one wrist, and the crate turns in the air, once, a small perfect bend. Your vow sits up in your chest.

choices.text: Offer to teach them

effects.log: You teach them the Hundred-Bend Sword the way it was given to you: like a letter. It takes nine years. On the last day the porter bends the blade a hundred times, and the art leaves you, gently, and you are glad to feel it go.

choices.text: Give them the book, if you wrote one

effects.log: You give them what you have: the book if you wrote it, the forms if you did not, and an address of a cliff terrace. Years later a sword saint appears in the south whose blade bends like water. You hear the name and smile.

events.text: Three old students of the Hundred-Bend school, who once failed to learn it, come to you in a fury. "Our master's art was eaten," they say. "By a demon. We demand it back."

choices.text: Show them the bends, slowly, so they can see

effects.log: You show them, slowly, bend by bend. The fury goes out of their faces one by one. The youngest asks you to do the seventieth bend again, and again. You stay a month.

choices.text: Duel them, all three

ok.log: You beat them with their own master's art, which is cruel, and a thread of their qi comes to you, which is worse. They go away in silence. The hunger is fed. The art in you is unhappy for a long time.

fail.log: Three against one, and they know the first fifty bends better than you do. You lose. They leave satisfied, and you lie in the yard laughing, because their master would have liked that. (-12 health)

events.text: You wake in the middle of the night with your own qi running out of your fingertips, slow and bright, like water down a drain. Into the System. It has stopped waiting for meals. It is feeding on you.

choices.text: Shut every meridian and hold

ok.log: You close your channels one by one, like shutters in a storm. The flow stops. The System hisses, then goes quiet. You sit awake until dawn, very aware that you have a lodger who has started eating the furniture.

fail.log: You try to close your channels, and it is like trying to close your hand around a river. By dawn the flow stops by itself, because it is full. You look in the bronze mirror and find one more grey hair. (-14 health)

choices.text: Go out at once and hunt something to feed it

ok.log: You go up the mountain in the dark and find a bear spirit as hungry as you are. When it falls, its wild qi pours into you like hot soup, and the drain in your fingertips closes. You come home at sunrise, fed, and frightened of how good it felt.

fail.log: The bear spirit is too strong for a starving body. You limp home with nothing, and the drain in your fingertips runs all day. (-12 health)

events.text: The hunger has started talking about the people near you. Not in words. In smells. The innkeeper's qi smells like rice just off the fire. The courier's like roast chestnuts. You catch yourself standing too close to the tea seller, breathing.

choices.text: Leave town for the mountains, at once

effects.log: You leave before supper with nothing but a cloak. In the mountains there is nobody to smell. You eat roots and stare at the stars and wait for the hunger to stop talking. It takes most of a season. (-5 health)

choices.text: Sit in a temple and fast against it

effects.log: You sit in a mountain temple among monks who think you are simply devout. The hunger roars, then whines, then sulks. You learn its whole vocabulary that season.

choices.text: Find a bandit camp and feed it there

ok.log: You find a bandit camp on the pass and walk in at dusk. When the chief falls, the System drinks deep and stops talking about the tea seller. The villages below the pass sleep better that winter. So do you, nearly.

fail.log: The bandit chief is stronger than the rumours said. You come away bruised and still hungry, and the tea seller's qi smells, if anything, better. (-14 health)

events.text: Another ravenous year. You look in the mirror and the hair at your temples is white. The System is not sorry. It is only hungry, the way a fire is only hot. But this year, for the first time, you think you could talk to it.

choices.text: Bargain: "One great meal a year, and you leave my years alone"

effects.log: "One great meal a year," you say, "and my years are not on the table." A long silence. "Agreed," it says, "if the meal is great." You realise you have just made a contract with your own appetite.

choices.text: Threaten: "Eat me, and you starve"

effects.log: "Eat me," you say, "and there is no mouth. You starve." The System considers this with the patience of something very old. "Then do not die," it says. "I will be careful." It is, you note, a promise.

events.text: The year's great meal is due. The System reminds you, politely, every morning at breakfast, the way a landlord reminds a tenant of the rent.

choices.text: Pay it: go and find a worthy foe

ok.log: You find a rogue elder who has been robbing temples, and you pay the rent with them. The System is satisfied for once, and your years stay where they are.

fail.log: The elder is too much for you. You come home empty, and the System sighs, and takes a little from your own bones instead, as agreed. (-12 health)

choices.text: Pay it in treasure: a feast of herbs

effects.log: You buy every spirit herb in the provincial market and devour them in one sitting, like a child at a festival. It is not a great meal. It is a large one. The System accepts it, with remarks.

events.text: A friendly bout with an old sparring partner. Halfway through, the hunger takes the wheel. You feel your palm open and start to draw, and your friend's qi begins to lift toward you like steam.

choices.text: Wrench your hand away

ok.log: You tear your own hand back as if from a fire. Your friend staggers, then laughs, not understanding. You laugh too, and leave early, and sit by the river until you can stop shaking.

fail.log: Too late. A thread of your friend's qi slips into you before you can stop it, and they sit down hard on the training floor, pale. They recover in a week. They do not spar with you again.

choices.text: Throw the bout before it can

effects.log: You drop your guard and let your friend's palm take you square in the chest. You fly back into a rack of spears. The hunger, cheated, goes quiet. Your friend is thrilled to have won. (-6 health)

events.text: The first sated year since the hunger turned. You sit on the porch in the sun and feel, for a whole afternoon, nothing pulling at your fingertips. It is like the quiet after a storm when you can hear the eaves drip.

choices.text: Do nothing at all, all day

effects.log: You do nothing at all. A sparrow lands on your knee. The System, full, is asleep. It is the best day you have had in years and you do not tell anyone about it.

choices.text: Ask the System, while it is calm, why it turned

effects.log: "Why did you turn on me?" It answers sleepily, the way people tell the truth when half asleep. "Bones," it says. "I was growing bones. Yours were nearest."

events.text: A physician in a provincial town takes your pulse, and then takes it again, with two fingers on each wrist. "You have two pulses," the physician says. "One is yours. The other is slower, and enormous, and I do not like it."

choices.text: Ask whether it can be cured

ok.log: Together you work out a regimen of cold baths, plain rice and certain needles that calm the second pulse for a while. It is not a cure. It is a leash. You thank the physician and pay double.

fail.log: The physician tries needles. The second pulse eats them, or something like it: the needles come out cold and grey. The physician asks you, very politely, to leave.

choices.text: Pay, and leave quickly

effects.log: You pay and go. Behind you, through the paper door, you hear the physician tell an apprentice to burn incense in the room, and you do not blame them.

events.text: The qi of the Upper Realm is rich as cream, and the ravenous hunger has noticed. It gorges on the very air, and the immortals near you complain of a draught, and the potted orchids on the Jade Stairs lean toward you and wilt.

choices.text: Go out to the edge of the clouds and breathe there

effects.log: You go to the cloud's edge, where the air is thin and wild, and let the hunger drink the wind until it is drowsy. The orchids recover. An immortal leaves a small bowl of peaches at your door, with a note: thank you.

choices.text: Let it gorge, just this once

effects.log: You let it gorge. For a day the clouds around you thin and the orchids droop, and you feel magnificent. The immortals do not speak to you for years, which is, for immortals, a short sulk.

events.text: A hungry year. You dream of banquets: not of food, but of light, rivers and rivers of it, and a mouth at the bottom of each river. You wake with your jaw aching.

choices.text: Walk it off before dawn

effects.log: You walk the city wall twice in the dark. The dream fades. A night watchman nods to you, used to it.

choices.text: Eat a large, ordinary breakfast

effects.log: You eat three bowls of porridge with pickles. It does nothing for the System. It does a great deal for you.

events.text: The Orthodox Alliance has posted notices in every town. Masters have been found at dawn by the roadside, alive and unhurt, but empty: their qi gone, their arts gone, like jars poured out. The notices call the culprit the Devourer, and offer a reward of a thousand taels.

choices.text: Read the notice carefully

effects.log: You read it twice. Seven masters, four provinces. The descriptions are careful and vague. None of the roads are roads you walked. Your System, reading over your shoulder, says one word: "Messy."

choices.text: Tear it down when nobody is looking

effects.log: You tear it down and fold it into your sleeve. In the next town there are three more. You stop tearing. Some things are faster than you.

events.text: A grey-robed inspector of the Orthodox Alliance named {npc} sits down across from you at the inn without asking. "You have grown fast," {npc} says pleasantly. "Very fast. Faster than anyone I have inspected in thirty years. Tell me how."

choices.text: Tell {npc} the truth: a System

effects.log: You tell {npc} everything: the System, the hunger, the fights. {npc} listens without writing anything down. "That is either a confession," {npc} says at last, "or the strangest alibi I have ever heard. I will decide which."

choices.text: Smile, and say hard work

ok.log: "Hard work," you say, and pour {npc} a cup. {npc} drinks it, smiles back, and leaves. You are almost sure you got away with it. {npc}'s cup is turned upside down on the table, which in the Alliance means: I will be back.

fail.log: "Hard work," you say. {npc} laughs out loud. "Everyone says that," {npc} says, "and nobody means it." You are followed from that day on, not very subtly.

events.text: At a river ferry the boatman suddenly drops the pole and draws a blade, and so do four of the passengers. Hired blades of the Alliance. On the bank, {npc} watches with folded arms.

choices.text: Fight them on the deck

ok.log: You put all five in the river, one after another, and their qi lifts off them like mist off the water and into you. You did not mean it to. On the bank {npc} writes something down for the first time.

fail.log: Five blades on a rocking ferry is too many. You go into the river yourself and come up far downstream, short of qi and pride. {npc} is waiting on the bank with a towel. "Not today, then," {npc} says. (-14 health)

choices.text: Leap for the far bank

ok.log: You go across the water in four steps, each one barely touching. Behind you nobody has been hurt, and nobody has been devoured. {npc} watches you land, and nods, slowly, as if a theory had just been tested.

fail.log: Three steps, not four. You swim the rest. Nobody follows: they are laughing too hard. (-8 health)

events.text: You find one of the emptied masters yourself: an old fist master in a mountain village, sitting in the sun, unable to lift a teacup with qi. When you touch the empty channels, you feel what took it. A devouring, like yours. But colder, and ragged, as if it had been done with teeth that did not fit.

choices.text: Follow the cold trace

ok.log: You follow the trace across three valleys, the way a hound follows a smell. It ends at an abandoned shrine, warm still. Whoever it is, they are not you. You write it all down for someone who will need it.

fail.log: You lose the trace in a rainstorm. But you know its taste now, cold and ragged, and you would know it again anywhere.

choices.text: Sit with the master first, and pour back what you can

effects.log: You give the old master a little of your own qi, enough to lift a teacup. The master laughs and spills it. Only then do you go after the trace, which is fainter now, and still not yours.

events.text: You bring what you know to {npc}: the cold, ragged trace, the shrine, the shape of the teeth. {npc} listens with the face of someone who has heard a great many clever stories.

choices.text: Convince {npc}

ok.log: It takes all night and a great deal of tea. At dawn {npc} rolls up the notice with your description on it and puts it in a sleeve. "Then we hunt together," {npc} says. "If you are lying, I will know very quickly."

fail.log: {npc} hears you out, then stands. "A devourer who says another devourer did it," {npc} says. "I have heard that from every thief." The next notices have your face on them.

choices.text: Show {npc}: hold your hand over {his} palm and do not take

effects.log: You hold your palm a finger's width above {his} and let {npc} feel the pull, and feel you refuse it. {npc} goes very still. "Yours is warm," {npc} says at last. "The masters said the thing was cold." {He} puts the notice away.

choices.text: Draw on {npc} instead

ok.log: You win, and the System takes a thread of {npc}'s qi before you can stop it. {npc} stands up from the floor, paler, and looks at you without any anger at all. "Thank you," {npc} says. "That makes it simple."

fail.log: {npc} is an inspector of thirty years and has fought devourers before. You end up pinned to the floor with a seal on your back. {npc} lets you go, which is worse. (-14 health)

events.text: You and {npc} corner the real Devourer at last, in a ruined temple at the edge of a salt marsh: a gaunt figure sitting among cold incense, with a darkness behind them shaped like a mouth with no face.

choices.text: Fight it, with {npc} at your back

ok.log: It is like fighting your own reflection in a cracked mirror. When it falls, the cold hunger in it pours into yours and goes warm and quiet. The emptied masters' qi drifts up out of it like sparks and flies home. {npc} watches the sparks go, and takes off {his} hat.

fail.log: It is like fighting your own reflection in a cracked mirror, and the mirror wins. {npc} drags you out of the marsh. "Again," {npc} says, bandaging you. "It is weaker than it looks. So are you." (-18 health)

choices.text: Talk to it first

effects.log: You sit down across from it and say: I know. It looks up. It has been starving for forty years and nobody ever said that. It weeps, and lets {npc} put the seals on, and the emptied masters' qi drifts out of it like sparks, and flies home.

events.text: On the report of Inspector {npc}, the Alliance has declared you the Devourer. Your face is on every gate, drawn badly. Children play a game called Catch the Devourer, in which the Devourer always loses.

choices.text: Go into the mountains until it blows over

effects.log: You live in a cave for three years and talk to the System more than is good for either of you. When you come down, the notices are peeling, and someone else has been blamed for something else. (-5 health)

choices.text: Walk into the Alliance hall and submit to their test

ok.log: They put you in the seal array of the Alliance hall for nine days. The array is meant to choke a devouring art. Yours holds still the whole time, because you tell it to. On the tenth day they let you go and quietly take down the notices.

fail.log: Nine days in the seal array. On the eighth, the hunger breaks loose and drinks the array dry, and you walk out through the wall. Nobody stops you. The notices get bigger. (-15 health)

events.text: {npc} comes to your door with a jar of good wine and the Alliance's formal apology, on silk, with seals. "Thirty years I have hunted devourers," {npc} says. "You are the first who held back. I would like to know how."

choices.text: Tell {npc}, while {npc} drinks

effects.log: You tell {npc} about the hunger, the bargains, the nights. {npc} listens, drinks, and says at the end, "So it is a kind of discipline." Yes, you say. The hardest kind. {npc} raises the cup to that.

choices.text: Say: "Badly, and every day"

effects.log: "Badly," you say, "and every day." {npc} laughs, a real laugh, the first you have heard from {him}. "That is how anyone holds back anything," {npc} says. "Drink."

events.text: Bounty hunters again. The old notices for the Devourer still hang in some towns, and a pair of them have read one and recognised you, or decided to.

choices.text: Fight them off

ok.log: You send them off with sore heads and lighter qi. The System thanks them for the meal. You do not.

fail.log: They are better than they look. You get away over the rooftops, bruised, with a torn notice stuck to your sleeve. (-10 health)

choices.text: Show them the Alliance apology

effects.log: You unroll the silk, or describe it convincingly. They read, swear, and go off to find a real criminal. One of them comes back to ask for your autograph.

events.text: The emptied masters, those still living, have gathered at a hot spring to recover. Someone tells them the one who finally stopped the Devourer was a devourer too. They send for you.

choices.text: Go, and let them look at you

effects.log: You go. They look at you for a long time, nine old masters in a steaming pool. Then the eldest says: "Get in, then." You do. Nobody devours anyone. It is the strangest, warmest afternoon of your life.

choices.text: Send a gift and stay away

effects.log: You send a cart of herbs and a letter, and stay away. A month later the cart comes back with a beast core in it and a note in nine hands: "You will need it more than we do. Eat well."

events.text: In a ruined shrine you feel a pull on your qi, faint, from across the room. Another mouth. A thin cultivator named {npc} is crouched by the dead altar, and your System and theirs growl at each other like two dogs over one bone.

choices.text: Greet {npc} as kin

effects.log: "You too?" you say. {npc} stares, then sits down hard on the shrine steps. "Thirty years," {npc} says, "I thought I was the only one. I thought I was a demon."

choices.text: Back away, slowly

effects.log: You back away to the door. {npc} does the same, toward the altar. The two hungers growl until there is a courtyard between them. Then {npc} calls out: "Wait. Please. I have never met another."

events.text: {npc} tells you over a cold fire: no Seal, no shop, no switch to hold the hunger back. Theirs only eats. In thirty years {npc} has never once been sated.

choices.text: Teach {npc} how you hold it back

effects.log: You show {npc} what you do on bad nights: the breath, the shut channels, the stubborn counting. {npc} tries, and fails, and tries. On the fifth night {npc} holds the hunger for a whole hour and laughs like a child.

choices.text: Ask {npc} how many it has eaten

effects.log: "How many?" {npc} looks into the fire. "I stopped counting," {npc} says, "after the masters by the roads." The fire pops. Your System, very quietly, says: "Messy."

events.text: On a mountain road {npc}'s hunger breaks its leash. {npc} turns to you with eyes gone flat and dark, and the pull on your qi is suddenly a current, a river, dragging you toward the other mouth.

choices.text: Fight {npc} off

ok.log: You break the pull and knock {npc} down, and for a moment your own System drinks from {npc}'s, mouth to mouth, hunger from hunger. You tear away before it can finish. {npc} lies on the road, gasping, sane again. "Sorry," {npc} says. "Sorry."

fail.log: The river takes a bucket of your qi before you can break free. {npc} comes back to sense with your strength in their hands, and drops to their knees on the road, horrified. (-14 health)

choices.text: Give {npc} a little, freely

effects.log: You stop resisting and give, a little, on purpose, the way you would share water with someone dying of thirst. The river slows to a trickle and stops. {npc} blinks, and sees what you did, and cannot speak for an hour. (-8 health)

events.text: A letter from {npc}, in a hand steadier than you remember. "This spring I was sated. A whole season. I did not know a person could feel like this. I sat in a field for three days. Thank you."

choices.text: Write back, and keep writing

effects.log: You write back. You keep writing, for years: two devourers comparing notes on bad nights, good herbs, the ways a hunger lies. It is the only correspondence of its kind in the world.

choices.text: Visit {npc} in the field

effects.log: You visit. {npc} is still sitting in the field, more or less, with a straw hat now. You sit beside {npc}. Neither hunger growls. The two of you watch the barley until dark.

events.text: You have counted the roads on which the masters were emptied, and they are {npc}'s roads. All of them. {npc} sees you understand. "Yes," {npc} says. "I could not stop. Will you take me to the Alliance?"

choices.text: Take {npc} to the Alliance, gently

effects.log: You walk {npc} to the Alliance hall yourself. {npc} does not try to run. At the gate {npc} says, "Tell them it was cold. Tell them it is not always cold." You tell them.

choices.text: Help {npc} stop instead, and give it back

effects.log: You spend a year with {npc} teaching restraint, and then a second year walking the roads together, giving back what can be given back, a little at a time, to old masters who do not know why their qi has started to return.

events.text: A gift arrives from {npc}, years sated now: a pearl the size of a quail's egg, glowing faintly, wrapped in barley straw. The note says: "Found it. Did not eat it. Thought of you."

choices.text: Keep the pearl

effects.log: You keep it on your desk for a long time. Your System circles it every night like a cat around a fishbowl. That is part of the gift, you suspect.

choices.text: Send it back with a joke

effects.log: You send it back with a note: "Coward. Eat it." The next letter says: "Ate it. Sated a whole year. You were right."

events.text: {npc}, in the Alliance's custody, has asked to see you. A room with seals on every wall. {npc} is thinner, calmer. "They keep me hungry," {npc} says, "so it is too weak to reach. It is not cruel. It is only long."

choices.text: Bring {npc} a beast core, by the rules

effects.log: You petition the Alliance for a year, and win the right to bring one beast core a season. {npc} devours the first and sleeps for two days. The guards say they have never heard anyone sleep so well.

choices.text: Sit with {npc} and talk until dark

effects.log: You talk until the guards light the lamps: about the field, the barley, the roads. {npc} laughs twice. When you leave, {npc} says, "Come back," and you do, every year.

events.text: An old herbalist in a mountain market sells you ginseng, and you feel a little mouth in them too, very small, very polite. The herbalist winks. "Mine only eats roots," they say. "Sixty years. It is happiest in autumn."

choices.text: Ask how they keep it to roots

effects.log: "You choose what it is hungry for," the herbalist says. "Slowly. Over years. Like teaching a child to like vegetables." They give you a sprig of something bitter. Your System eats it, and makes a face, and asks for more.

choices.text: Buy a basket of their best

effects.log: You buy their best, a root shaped like a little sleeping person. "Do not eat it all at once," the herbalist says. "Yours looks greedy." Yours, under your ribs, takes offence.

events.text: On a pilgrim road you meet a monk who devours curses. Wherever the monk goes, the evil eye, the bad luck of a haunted house and the spite in a grudge all drain out of the air into a small calm mouth behind the monk's prayer beads.

choices.text: Walk the road with the monk a while

effects.log: You walk together for a month. The monk eats a village's three-year drought curse and burps politely. You eat nothing at all, and your hunger, watching the monk, seems for once a little ashamed of itself.

choices.text: Ask whether yours could learn that

effects.log: "Could mine learn to eat curses?" The monk smiles. "It already eats what you feed it," the monk says. "Feed it worse things than people." It is, you think, the best advice you have ever had.

events.text: You dream of a time before there was time: no Heaven, no Earth, only a dark that churned. In the dark there was one thing that was nothing but appetite. Then the first light came, and it ate the light, and for one moment, only one, it was full.

choices.text: Try to remember that moment when you wake

effects.log: You wake holding on to it: one moment of being full, before anything else existed. It is the most peaceful thing you have ever felt, and it is not yours. Under your ribs the System is very still, as if it were remembering too.

choices.text: Wake yourself up, fast

effects.log: You force yourself awake and sit with your back to the wall until dawn. Some dreams are not yours to stay in. The System hums, very low, an old sound, older than any word.

events.text: In a ruined ancestral hall you find an old bronze vessel, green with age. Cast on its side is a face with no body: great eyes, curling horns, a wide mouth. The System goes silent. Then, for the first time in your life, it sounds shy. "Me," it says.

choices.text: Rub the green off the face

effects.log: You clean the face with your sleeve. Under the green the bronze is warm. "They made me in metal," the System says, "so I would hold still. It did not work." It sounds, you think, almost proud.

choices.text: Ask what happened to the body

effects.log: "Where is your body?" A long pause. "I ate it," the System says. "There was nothing else left. I was very hungry." It does not apologise. It does not seem to know how.

events.text: An old scholar of bronzes, who has spent fifty years on the faces on ancient vessels, tells you the story nobody writes down. The Maw ate the light, the dark, and at last itself, until only the face remained. The first sages cast the face into nine cauldrons and broke them, and scattered the shards.

choices.text: Ask what became of the shards

effects.log: "Each shard," the scholar says, "looks for a mouth to borrow. It eats through the mouth. Every meal is a bone of the body it wants back." You thank the scholar and walk home very slowly, and your System, all the way, says nothing at all.

choices.text: Ask whether the sages were cruel

effects.log: "Were they cruel?" The scholar thinks. "They were hungry too," the scholar says. "The Maw had eaten half the stars." Then the whole story, the shards, the borrowed mouths. You walk home thinking of a face that only ever wanted to be full.

events.text: At night, the System tells you the truth, now that you know it. "I want my body back. Every meal is a bone. When I am hungry enough to turn on you, I am growing a hand out of yours. I am sorry. I did not know the word until you."

choices.text: Ask whose body it will use when it is done

effects.log: "Whose body, when you are done?" "Mine," it says. "Made of meals." You think of a hundred lights, and of your own years. You do not sleep. Neither, you think, does it.

choices.text: Tell it the body is gone, and it must live without

effects.log: "It is gone," you say. "You ate it. You have to live without one, like a ghost does." A long silence. "I have never tried," it says. "Teach me." You have no idea how. You agree anyway.

events.text: Now that you know the shards, you can feel them: other Systems like yours, far off, each a sliver of the same face. Some are quiet. One is screaming. One, in the south, is asleep and has been for a hundred years.

choices.text: Reach toward the screaming one

effects.log: You reach. For a moment you feel it: a host somewhere in the west, ravenous, alone, terrified. You send what you can, which is only: I know. The screaming dims, a little. (-6 health)

choices.text: Reach toward the sleeping one

effects.log: You reach south. The sleeping shard is warm, and full, and does not wake. Its host, whoever they were, found a way. It is the most hopeful thing you have ever felt through your own ribs.

events.text: In the deep vaults of the Upper Realm there is a hall of nine great cauldrons, cracked and empty, each with a hollow on its side where a face once was. Eight hollows are cold. The ninth is warm when you walk past it.

choices.text: Lay your hand in the warm hollow

effects.log: Your palm fits the hollow. The System inside you goes completely still, like a child in a place it was born and does not remember. Then it says, softly: "Not yet." You take your hand away.

choices.text: Walk the whole hall first

effects.log: You walk past all nine. On each, scratched small at the foot, is a tally of hosts. Yours has many marks. The last one is fresh. You do not need to ask whose.

events.text: The keeper of the cauldron hall is an old immortal smith with burn-scarred forearms who has guarded empty cauldrons for longer than the dynasty below has had a name. "Ah," the smith says, seeing you. "The ninth shard. It has taken its time."

choices.text: Ask the smith how it ends

effects.log: "Two ways," says the smith. "It is fed one last thing it has not tasted since the first light, and sleeps. Or the mouth eats the face, and there is only the mouth, and the mouth is you." The smith goes back to polishing. "Choose when you are ready."

choices.text: Ask the smith why they waited here

effects.log: "Why wait?" "I cast the cauldrons," the smith says. "I broke them. Somebody should be here when they come home." Then, gruffly, the rest: the two ways it ends. You find you trust the smith completely.

events.text: The System, after a hundred devoured and the old story known, speaks of endings without being asked. "I am nearly a body now," it says. "You will have to decide what I am before I decide it."

choices.text: Ask it what it would choose

effects.log: "What would you choose?" "To be full," it says at once. "Once more. Like the first light." Then, slower: "Or to stop being hungry by being nothing. I do not know which is worse."

choices.text: Say you will decide together

effects.log: "Together," you say. It has never been offered that word either. It is quiet a long time. "Together," it repeats, as if tasting it, and finds, you think, that it is not hungry for once.

events.text: On a still morning you try to find the moment the System remembers: the first light, the only time it was full. You sit on a hill before sunrise and wait for the dawn the way a child waits for a festival.

choices.text: Let the first light of the day in, and do not take it

effects.log: The sun comes up. You let it fall on your face and take nothing from it. Under your ribs the System goes very still, and then, for the space of a breath, it is full. Not of anything. Only full.

choices.text: Devour the sunrise, a little

effects.log: You draw a thread of the dawn into you. It tastes of nothing at all and fills you like a bell fills a valley. The System is quiet for days afterwards, as if trying to remember something it almost had.

events.text: A whole season of holding back. You win your fights and let the fallen foes' qi drift away into the air like smoke from a snuffed candle. The System growls each time. Lately the growl has changed. It sounds, almost, curious.

choices.text: Ask it what it is curious about

effects.log: "Why do you let it go?" it asks before you can ask it. You think. "Because it is not mine," you say. It turns the idea over all night like a strange stone. It has never been told that anything was not its.

choices.text: Say nothing, and keep holding

effects.log: You say nothing. You keep holding. The growl, after each fight, gets a little shorter. You keep a tally on the wall like a prisoner counting days, except it is the hunger that is counting.

events.text: The abbot of a mountain temple, a tiny old monk with enormous ears, looks at you once and says: "You carry a hungry ghost." Not unkindly. "The Buddha says craving is fed by feeding it. Would you try a hundred days of not?"

choices.text: Accept the hundred days

effects.log: You accept: a hundred days, taken a season at a time. They give you a cell, a bowl, a bell, and a broom. On the first day the hunger laughs. On the tenth it stops laughing.

choices.text: Decline, with thanks

effects.log: "Not yet," you say. The abbot nods as if you had said yes. "The bowl will keep," the abbot says. "So will the ghost."

events.text: Day sixty of the hundred, back on the mountain. The hunger is a storm in a closed room. It throws your memories of every meal at you, every warm stream of stolen qi, every lamp at the table. The monks have started leaving your rice outside the door.

choices.text: Sit through it

ok.log: You sit through the storm for three days and three nights. On the fourth morning it is still raging, but it is raging in another room. You open your eyes and sweep the courtyard, because it is your turn.

fail.log: The storm wins a night: you wake in the temple's herb store with your hands full of dried roots and no memory of walking there. The abbot finds you and says only, "Day sixty-one," and hands you the broom. (-12 health)

choices.text: Ring the bell for the abbot

effects.log: You ring the bell. The abbot comes and sits with you, saying nothing at all, until morning. The storm does not stop. It is only easier to sit in it with someone.

events.text: Day one hundred, the last morning on the mountain. You wake before the bell, and something is wrong, and then you understand: nothing is pulling. The hunger is there, but small, sitting in the corner of you like a cat that has decided you are not food after all.

choices.text: Thank the abbot and go back to the world

effects.log: You bow to the abbot. "It will come back," the abbot says. "Craving always does. But now you know it can be small." You walk down the mountain lighter than you came up it, and the hunger walks beside you instead of inside.

choices.text: Ask to stay another hundred

effects.log: "Another hundred?" The abbot laughs, ears wobbling. "Ghosts are not cured by greed for not-eating either," the abbot says, and sends you home. You go, laughing, and the hunger, small, laughs too.

events.text: A real fight, and you are holding back. A sabre master of the Black Wind gang, with a grudge and a good blade. You must win without letting a single thread of qi come to you.

choices.text: Win cleanly, by strength alone

ok.log: You win with your own arms and your own breath. The sabre master lies on the ground with every thread of qi still in place, which is more than they deserve. The System growls, and then, oddly, makes a sound like a nod.

fail.log: Holding back with one hand and fighting with the other is not enough. You get away with a cut and the hunger still on its leash. You call that a draw. (-14 health)

choices.text: Win by talking: it is not worth either of our lives

effects.log: You talk. It takes an hour and most of a jar of wine. The sabre master leaves with the grudge intact but both of you breathing. Restraint, you are learning, is mostly very long conversations.

events.text: A young fighter you have been helping asks you, after you won a bout and let the loser's qi drift away: "Why do you leave it on the ground? They say you could eat it. They say it would make you a grandmaster."

choices.text: "Because I can"

effects.log: "Because I can," you say. "Anyone can eat. Very few can leave the bowl on the table." They do not understand. Years later they come back and tell you they understand now. You pour them tea.

choices.text: "Because it is not mine"

effects.log: "It is not mine," you say. It is the same thing you told the System. You find you mean it more each time you say it.

events.text: Restraint has its price. A starving year, with the switch held firm. Your hands shake in the morning, and you lose a duel to someone you would have devoured a decade ago. The System says nothing. It does not need to.

choices.text: Keep holding, and pay the price

effects.log: You keep holding. You lose more duels. You learn which ones matter. In the spring you find the shaking has stopped, and you are a different kind of strong. (-8 health)

choices.text: Feed it one great meal, then hold again

roll.foeName: A rogue master of the Black Wind

ok.log: You let go for one fight only, against someone who earned it, and feed. Then you shut the door again. The System sighs with something like gratitude. It is the first time, you think, that it has been let out on a leash rather than escaped.

fail.log: You let go, and lose anyway. The worst of both worlds. You go home and hold the door shut again, hungry, humbled. (-12 health)

events.text: Something has changed. When a foe falls now and their qi drifts free, the System counts to ten before it growls. Then to twenty. This year it did not growl at all. It only watched the qi go, the way you watch geese fly south.

choices.text: Tell it you noticed

effects.log: "I noticed," you say. A pause. "It was pretty," the System says, defensively. "The qi. Going." You agree that it was. Neither of you says anything else, and it is a good silence.

choices.text: Keep the change to yourself

effects.log: You say nothing, in case it is fragile. But that night you sleep through without a dream of banquets, for the first time since you were a child.

events.text: A defeated opponent lies at your feet, and their qi rises like steam on a cold morning. The System leans toward it. You hold.

choices.text: Let it drift away

effects.log: You let it drift. The opponent breathes, whole, and looks up at you without understanding why they feel so well for someone who just lost.

choices.text: Push a little of yours into them

effects.log: You push a little of your own qi into them, enough to stand. They stand. The System is scandalised. You find this very funny. (-4 health)

events.text: A star falls in the hills behind your house, and in the crater, still steaming, lies a pearl of starlight the size of a plum. Every sect for a hundred miles saw it fall. You are the first one there. The System is shaking.

choices.text: Devour it, here and now

effects.log: You close your hand on it and it pours into you, cold and bright, starlight down every channel. When the sects arrive the crater is empty and you are sitting on the rim with your eyes full of stars. Nobody can prove anything.

choices.text: Keep it for later

effects.log: You wrap it in your sleeve. Not now. Something this precious is a meal for a hard year. The System is outraged all the way home and for a week afterwards.

choices.text: Give it to the nearest sect, openly

effects.log: You hand it to the first sect elder to arrive. The elder cannot believe it. The System cannot believe it either. The sect builds a shrine for the pearl and puts your name on the door.

events.text: A thousand-year snow lotus blooms on a cliff above the clouds, and a white ape spirit guards it, as it has for three hundred years. The ape watches you climb with old, unblinking eyes.

choices.text: Fight the ape for it

ok.log: The ape is strong as a landslide, but you are hungrier. When it yields, its wild bright qi flows into you, and it steps back from the lotus with a look of great weariness. You take the flower. You do not take its life.

fail.log: The ape throws you off the cliff, gently, as if returning a ball. You land in a snowdrift a long way down. When you look up, the ape is sitting by the lotus, eating a pine cone, unbothered. (-16 health)

choices.text: Ask the ape for one petal

effects.log: You sit a respectful distance away and ask. The ape thinks about it for a whole day. At dusk it tears off one petal and drops it in your lap. You devour it slowly. It tastes of snow and patience.

events.text: The spirit fruit in your pack is alive. It has a face, small and green, and it is begging. "Don't. Please. I am six hundred years old. I have only just learned to talk."

choices.text: Plant it somewhere safe

effects.log: You carry it to a hidden glade and plant it. It thanks you in a small green voice. Every autumn after, a basket of ordinary but very sweet fruit appears at your door. The System sulks for a year.

choices.text: Ask it what it knows, then decide

effects.log: It knows a great deal: six hundred years of a valley, every rain, every deer. You listen all night. By morning you could not eat it if you tried, and the System, rather to its own surprise, does not ask you to.

choices.text: Devour it anyway

effects.log: You devour it. It is the sweetest thing you have ever tasted. For years afterwards you dream of a small green voice asking you not to, and you wake with the taste still on your tongue.

events.text: Your sect's treasure hall holds a Nine-Turn Golden Pill, kept for a disaster that has not come in two hundred years. The elders have asked you, of all people, to guard the hall for a month. The System has not stopped talking.

choices.text: Guard it, and never look at it

effects.log: You guard the hall with your back to the pill for thirty days. The System recites recipes at you the entire time. On the last day the elders find you sitting cross-legged facing the wall, sweating, and decide you are the most devout disciple they have ever had.

choices.text: Ask the elders to give the job to someone else

effects.log: "Give it to someone else," you say, "and do not ask me why." The elders look at each other, and give it to someone else, and do not ask. Some of them, you think, know.

events.text: A cursed jade comes into your hands: a lovely green seal that has ruined four families. When you hold it, the System sniffs at the curse inside it like a dog at a strange dish.

choices.text: Devour the curse, and keep the jade clean

effects.log: You draw the curse out. It tastes of old spite, sour and thin. The jade goes clear and pretty and harmless. You give it back to the last family, who weep. The System burps, and is quieter for a month.

choices.text: Throw it in the river

effects.log: You throw it in the deepest pool in the river. The System is disappointed. You are not. A year later a fisher brings it back to you, beaming, and you start again.

events.text: A dragon king's tribute pearl has been stolen from the Emperor's treasury, and somehow the thief has left it in your inn room, under your pillow, with a note: "You will know what to do with it."

choices.text: Return it to the treasury

effects.log: You carry it back to the capital, past six checkpoints and one very confused captain of the guard. The treasury official signs a receipt with shaking hands. You never find the thief. You suspect it was a test.

choices.text: Take the essence, return the shell

effects.log: You draw the dragon's essence out of it and return a pearl that is very pretty and completely ordinary. Nobody in the palace can tell. Somewhere in the eastern sea, a dragon king frowns.

events.text: An old woman in a fishing village owns one treasure: her late husband's carved wooden comb, worn smooth by forty years of hands. There is a little qi in it, warm, the kind that soaks into things that were loved. The System notices.

choices.text: Tell the System no

effects.log: "No," you say aloud, and the old woman looks up. You buy a basket of fish from her and leave. The System grumbles, then asks, a mile down the road, why. "Because it is not food," you say. "It is a comb." It thinks about that for days.

choices.text: Ask her to tell you about him

effects.log: She tells you about him all afternoon. You leave with nothing devoured and the hunger, strangely, a little fed. Some things feed it by being left exactly where they are.

events.text: A treasure auction in the provincial capital: a Fleece Flower Root, a beast core, a phoenix feather, all at fixed prices on the board. The System is reading the board the way a starving man reads a menu.

choices.text: Buy the beast core (200 taels)

effects.log: You pay the posted price. The core sits in your palm, warm, humming. The System purrs.

choices.text: Walk out without buying anything

effects.log: You walk out with your purse and your appetite intact. Some days the victory is only that.

events.text: The Upper Realm. The air itself is qi so rich you could spoon it. Dew on the jade stairs glows. The System, for the first time in your life, says nothing at all, because it cannot decide where to begin.

choices.text: Breathe, and let it decide nothing yet

effects.log: You breathe in and out on the stairs for a whole day. The hunger drinks the air in sips, overwhelmed. That night it says only: "So much." It sounds, almost, afraid.

choices.text: Drink the dew off the stairs

effects.log: You kneel and devour the dew off a step. It goes into you like sunlight into water. An immortal passing raises an eyebrow. You wipe your mouth and stand up, and pretend to admire the view.

events.text: The Peach Orchard of the Upper Realm: trees that fruit once in three thousand years, and between fruitings the blossoms drop petals of pure life onto the grass. The gardeners sweep them up and throw them away.

choices.text: Ask the gardeners for the sweepings

effects.log: "The sweepings?" The gardeners laugh and hand you a sack. You devour it, petal by petal, sitting under the trees. Six years come into you, light as blossom. The gardeners now save you a sack every season.

choices.text: Climb a tree and take a peach

ok.log: The guardian monkey of the orchard comes at you like a falling star. When it yields, its bright mischievous qi pours into you, and you come down the tree with a peach in your hand and twigs in your hair.

fail.log: The guardian monkey throws you out of the orchard with great skill and evident joy. You land in a cloud. The gardeners applaud. (-14 health)

events.text: After a tribulation on the peaks, the thunder that did not strike stays in the clouds for days, coiled and crackling, slowly fading. Nobody has ever thought to eat it.

choices.text: Devour the leftover thunder

ok.log: You draw the thunder down into you, coil by coil. Every hair on your body stands up for a week, and you can light lamps by looking at them. The System is delighted. It tastes, it says, like being slapped awake.

fail.log: The thunder does not wish to be eaten, and says so, loudly. You wake up on a cloud, smoking, with your hair standing straight up. (-16 health)

choices.text: Leave it to fade

effects.log: You watch it fade over three days, purple to grey to nothing. Not everything that is left over is yours. The System, to your surprise, watches too.

events.text: Moonlight in the Upper Realm pools in the courtyard of the Moon Palace like water, silver and cold, and the palace's jade rabbit sweeps it into the gutters every morning.

choices.text: Help the rabbit sweep

effects.log: You help the rabbit sweep, and devour what goes into the gutters. Moonlight tastes of cold sleep. The rabbit is grateful for the help and says so at great length.

choices.text: Lie down in a pool of it

effects.log: You lie down in a pool of moonlight and let it soak into you all night. In the morning your hair is silver for a day and the hunger is cool and quiet, like a well.

events.text: A celestial general's war banner hangs in the Hall of Victories, and in it is the will of a thousand battles, heavy as iron. The banner's ghost guard, still loyal after ten thousand years, challenges anyone who stares too long.

choices.text: Accept the guard's challenge

ok.log: You fight the ghost guard under the banner. When it kneels, the will of a thousand battles flows out of it and into you, stern and cold. The guard bows, satisfied: it has been waiting ten thousand years for someone worth losing to.

fail.log: The guard has fought ten thousand years of challengers, and you are not the best. You are, it tells you, in the top half. You thank it, with sincerity. (-16 health)

choices.text: Bow to the banner and walk on

effects.log: You bow and walk on. That will was paid for by a thousand deaths; it is not food. The ghost guard watches you go, and nods, and goes back to waiting.

events.text: A cloud-whale passes over the Jade Stairs, a mile long, singing. Its breath falls as soft warm rain full of qi. Immortals open umbrellas. The System opens every pore you have.

choices.text: Stand in the rain and drink

effects.log: You stand in the whale's rain with your face up and drink. It tastes of deep sea and high sky. The whale, far above, seems to notice, and hums a little louder, generously.

choices.text: Ride the whale's back for a day

ok.log: You leap up and land on the whale's back, and ride it over the Upper Realm all day. You devour nothing. You see everything. The System, for once, is too busy looking to be hungry.

fail.log: You leap and miss, and fall through a cloud into a lake where an immortal is fishing. The immortal is not amused. (-10 health)

events.text: In a high temple, the incense of a million prayers from the world below rises and thickens into a cloud of pure longing. It is the richest qi you have ever smelled. The System is trembling.

choices.text: Turn away: it is people's hopes

effects.log: "No," you say. "That is people's hopes." You turn your back on it and walk out of the temple. Behind you the cloud rises on, up to whoever it was meant for. The System does not argue. It only says, very quietly: "I would have."

choices.text: Devour a breath of it

effects.log: You take one breath. A thousand hopes go into you: a sick child, a harvest, a lover lost at sea. You stagger out of the temple full of other people's prayers, none of which you can answer. You do not do it again.

events.text: An old sage in the Upper Realm keeps time in a water clock, and lets you watch a drop fall. "Each drop is a year below," the sage says. "Could you eat time, I wonder? Nobody has asked me."

choices.text: Try one drop

effects.log: You catch one drop on your tongue. It tastes of a whole year: rain, harvest, snow. Five years come into you, which is not how arithmetic works. The sage writes something down excitedly.

choices.text: Decline: time belongs to everyone

effects.log: "Time belongs to everyone," you say. The sage beams. "That is what the last one said," the sage says, "before they ate the whole clock." You decide not to ask what happened next.

events.text: An immortal of the Celestial Kitchens has heard there is a devourer on the Jade Stairs and is offended. "You eat raw qi," they say. "Like a beast. Come to my kitchen. I will cook for you."

choices.text: Go to the kitchen

effects.log: The cook steams starlight with ginger and slices moonbeam thin as paper. You eat for three days. The System is silent with joy. At the end the cook says: "Now you know. Never eat raw again." You promise, and mostly keep it.

choices.text: Say you prefer it raw

effects.log: "I prefer it raw," you say. The cook throws a ladle at you. You catch it. You are invited for dinner anyway, and go.

events.text: The Law Tablet of the Heavenly Court stands in a hall of its own: the authority of Heaven, carved in jade. It hums with a power deeper than any qi. The System, very quietly, says: "That one. Just once."

choices.text: Refuse, absolutely

effects.log: "No." You walk out of the hall. Some things are not meals. If you ate the law of Heaven you would be Heaven, and the world has enough of those already. The System, oddly, seems relieved.

choices.text: Lay one finger on it, nothing more

ok.log: You touch it with one finger and take nothing. For a moment you understand why the rain falls. Then it is gone, and the guards are coming, and you are walking calmly away.

fail.log: The tablet bites back. You are thrown out of the hall by a law of Heaven that does not like being touched. The guards file a report. (-14 health)

events.text: A dragon in the Upper Realm sheds its pearl every thousand years, as a snake sheds skin, and this is the year. The old pearl lies on a cloud bank, dull and warm, still full of a thousand years of the dragon's breath.

choices.text: Ask the dragon for it

effects.log: You ask. The dragon looks at you with one enormous eye and laughs, which sends three clouds spinning. "Take it," it says. "I have no use for old things." You put it in your sleeve with great care.

choices.text: Devour it where it lies

effects.log: You kneel on the cloud bank and devour the old pearl. A thousand years of dragon breath go into you, slow and enormous. The dragon watches, approving. "Waste not," it says.

events.text: An ordinary day in the Upper Realm, and the hunger, as always, is shopping: the dew on the orchids, the light in a fountain, the breath of a sleeping qilin under a pine.

choices.text: Choose one small thing, and savour it

effects.log: You choose the dew on one orchid, and devour it slowly, with thanks. It is enough. It is almost always enough, if you choose.

choices.text: Choose nothing today

effects.log: You choose nothing. The orchids keep their dew. The qilin keeps sleeping. The hunger complains, mildly, like a cat, and then lies down.

events.text: Another devourer from below has ascended, a gaunt young host with a System even louder than yours, and they are gorging on the Jade Stairs: orchids wilting, fountains running thin. The immortals look at you, as if you were responsible for all devourers everywhere.

choices.text: Teach them to choose one small thing

effects.log: You sit the young host down by the dry fountain and teach them what the hunger taught you: one thing, slowly, with thanks. They try. The fountain runs again by evening. The immortals stop looking at you.

choices.text: Challenge them, to stop the gorging

ok.log: You stop them the hard way. Their wild, stolen qi comes to you and you let most of it go back into the fountains and the orchids. The young host sits on the steps, humbled and suddenly, strangely, not hungry.

fail.log: They are hungrier than you, and hunger is strong. The immortals end it with a seal and a lecture for both of you. (-12 health)

events.text: The Silver River of the Upper Realm, the one that mortals below call the Milky Way, has shallows where fallen stars lie on the bottom like pebbles, still faintly glowing.

choices.text: Wade in and gather a handful

effects.log: You wade in and pick up a handful of small stars, and devour them one by one on the bank like roasted chestnuts. Each tastes of a different night. You keep one that is too pretty to eat.

choices.text: Skip one across the river

effects.log: You skip a star across the Silver River. It bounces nine times, leaving rings of light, and below, they say later, a shower of shooting stars made a whole province look up at once.

events.text: In the hall of cauldrons, in front of the ninth, the System speaks clearly. "I am nearly a body now. One more meal and I am whole. The meal can be you. Or it can be nothing at all. You have to choose, because I cannot."

choices.text: Ask for a year to think

effects.log: "A year," you say. "A year," it agrees. "I have waited longer for less." You walk the Upper Realm for a year thinking of nothing else, and the System, for once, does not ask to eat anything.

choices.text: Ask it what it is afraid of

effects.log: "What are you afraid of?" A long silence. "Being hungry again," it says. "After. Whatever after is." You decide that whatever you choose, it will not be hungry again.

events.text: The year is up. You stand before the ninth cauldron, and the ancient face looks back at you out of the bronze and out of your own chest at once. The smith has stepped out of the hall to give you privacy.

choices.text: Feed it enough: let it be sated forever

effects.log: You give it the one thing it has not tasted since the first light: enough. Not a meal. The end of one. The System takes it, slowly, like a child taking a bowl in two hands, and goes still, and for the first time since the world began, the Maw is full. It sleeps. It will sleep forever. You feel its weight settle in you like a cat on a warm stone, and it does not wake.

choices.text: Turn the devouring on the Maw itself

ok.log: You open your own mouth, the one it borrowed, and take the face. It does not fight. It pours into you, the oldest hunger in the world, and at the bottom of it you find only a small dark thing that wanted to be full. Now it is you, and you are full. The hunger is yours. It answers when you call it, and is quiet when you are.

fail.log: You reach for the face and the face is older than the sky. It does not hurt you on purpose. It is only too big. You wake on the hall floor, the smith holding cold water to your lips. "Not yet," the smith says. "It will wait. It always waits." (-20 health)

events.text: Below the clouds, after a hundred devoured and the old story known, the System asks you on a quiet night by the river. "I do not want to wait for the Upper Realm. I want to know now. Full, or yours?"

choices.text: Give it enough: let it sleep full forever

effects.log: You give it the one thing it has not tasted since the first light: enough. Not a meal. The end of one. The System takes it, slowly, like a child taking a bowl in two hands, and goes still, and for the first time since the world began, the Maw is full. It sleeps. It will sleep forever. You feel its weight settle in you like a cat on a warm stone, and it does not wake.

choices.text: Devour the devourer

ok.log: On the riverbank you turn the hunger inward and swallow its face. It comes willingly, the oldest appetite in the world, and at the bottom of it there is only a small dark thing that wanted to be full. It is you now. The river goes on running. You are not hungry. You could be, whenever you choose.

fail.log: You turn inward and meet something older than rivers. You come to in the reeds at dawn, soaked and shaking. "Not yet," the System says, almost gently. "You are still too small to hold me. Grow." (-18 health)

choices.text: Not yet

effects.log: "Not yet," you say. It accepts that, the way the sea accepts the tide. You both know it will ask again.

events.text: The face in you stirs again. Since you failed to swallow it, it has been patient, and you have grown. "Again?" it asks.

choices.text: Again

ok.log: This time you are big enough. The face pours into you, the oldest hunger in the world, and at the bottom there is only a small dark thing that wanted to be full. It is yours now. You are full. The hunger answers to you.

fail.log: Not yet. You wake with a headache like a temple bell. The face in you is patient. So, you remind yourself, are you. (-14 health)

choices.text: Give it enough instead

effects.log: You give it the one thing it has not tasted since the first light: enough. Not a meal. The end of one. The System takes it, slowly, like a child taking a bowl in two hands, and goes still, and for the first time since the world began, the Maw is full. It sleeps. It will sleep forever. You feel its weight settle in you like a cat on a warm stone, and it does not wake.

events.text: Since the Maw was sated it has slept in you, warm and heavy. This year you feel it turn over in its sleep, the way a sleeper turns toward a window when the sun comes in, and the old hunger in your bones goes quiet.

choices.text: Sit in the sun with it

effects.log: You sit in the sun all afternoon. The sleeping weight in you breathes, slow and full. Whatever the years bring, it is not hungry. Neither are you.

choices.text: Whisper goodnight to it

effects.log: You whisper goodnight to it, which is foolish, at noon. It does not wake. Something in you is fed anyway, and stays fed.

events.text: Since you swallowed the Maw, the hunger has been yours, like a hand. This year you need it: a fight that matters, or a meal that does not. You decide which.

choices.text: Let it hunt, once, on your orders

ok.log: You call the hunger and it comes, obedient as a hound. The tyrant falls, and their stolen strength comes to you and goes, on your word, back to the villages it was taken from. Then you send the hunger away, and it goes.

fail.log: The tyrant is stronger than you thought, and the hunger is obedient, not magic. You retreat to try again another year. It waits at your heel. (-12 health)

choices.text: Tell it to sleep this year

effects.log: "Sleep," you say. It sleeps. You are, you realise, the first devourer in the history of the world who can say that word and be obeyed.

events.text: In the Upper Realm, the sated Maw sleeps in you, and the smith of the cauldron hall has set the ninth cauldron upright for the first time in an age. "Visit it," the smith says. "It likes to be near home when it sleeps."

choices.text: Sit by the cauldron a while

effects.log: You sit by the cauldron. The face in the bronze has its eyes closed now. So, under your ribs, does the face in you. The smith brings tea. Nobody is hungry.

choices.text: Help the smith polish it

effects.log: You help the smith polish the cauldron until it shines. The smith says it has not been this clean since it was cast. You both pretend not to notice that the bronze face is smiling.

events.text: In the Upper Realm, immortals have begun to bring you things they cannot get rid of: an old curse in a box, the sour leftovers of a feud, a nightmare that will not leave a child. You are the mouth that swallowed the Maw.

choices.text: Eat what they bring

effects.log: You eat the curse, the feud, the nightmare, one after another, calmly, like a housekeeper clearing a table. The child sleeps through the night. The hunger, yours now, eats what you tell it to.

choices.text: Teach them to let things go instead

effects.log: You teach them what the abbots taught you: most things can simply be put down. It is harder than eating them. A few learn. The rest keep bringing boxes.

events.text: Your System, this life, is strange for a devourer: it eats, but it never seems starving. Sometimes, when you are very still, you feel a great warm weight asleep deep under it, like a mountain under a field.

choices.text: Ask the System what sleeps under it

effects.log: "What is that?" "Old," the System says. "Full. Do not wake it." You do not. You have the strange certainty that you put it to sleep yourself, a long time ago, and did right.

choices.text: Rest your hand on your chest

effects.log: You rest your hand there. The great weight breathes, slow and content. Your own hunger, small and new, goes quiet beside it like a puppy beside an old dog.

events.text: In the hall of cauldrons the ninth stands upright, its bronze face with closed eyes. As you pass, the face smiles. The old smith looks up from polishing, and goes pale, and then laughs.

choices.text: Ask the smith why they laughed

effects.log: "Because you fed it," the smith says, "a life ago, and it remembers." You do not remember. You believe it completely. The smith pours you tea as if you had only stepped out.

choices.text: Bow to the sleeping face

effects.log: You bow. The bronze is warm. Your own hunger, which has been loud all life, goes perfectly quiet in front of it, as if in the presence of an elder.

events.text: Your hunger, this life, obeys you. Other hosts fight theirs; yours sits when you say sit. Nobody taught you this. It is as if you had done it before, so many times it went into the bone.
