choices.text: Test it: call it, then dismiss it

effects.log: You call it and it comes; you dismiss it and it goes. The System says, uneasily: "I do not know why I do that." You do not either. You suspect the soul remembers swallowing something very old.

choices.text: Let it be, and be grateful

effects.log: You let it be. A hunger that obeys is a gift you did not earn in this life. Perhaps you earned it in another.

events.text: In the hall of cauldrons the ninth hollow is empty and cold, and the old smith, seeing you, sets down the polishing cloth. "So," the smith says. "The one who ate it. Hungry again, are you?"

choices.text: Say: "Only a little"

effects.log: "Only a little," you say. The smith laughs until the cauldrons ring. "The first time," the smith says, "you said: not at all." You do not remember. You find you are proud of yourself anyway.

choices.text: Ask what you were like

effects.log: "Quiet," the smith says. "Full. You came here after and sat with the empty cauldron for a hundred years, as if keeping it company." You sit with it a while now, for old times' sake.

events.text: On a stormy night, as the clouds gather over your roof, you see faint lights in them, a hundred or so, like lanterns far away. They do not come down. They seem to be looking for someone, and to have found them.

choices.text: Wave to them

effects.log: You wave, feeling foolish. The lights brighten, all at once, and the rain that falls is warm. In the morning your hunger is quieter than it has been in years.

choices.text: Open your arms, as if returning something

effects.log: You open your arms. Nothing leaves you. But you feel, very strongly, that something once did, and that it was right, and that the sky has not forgotten.

events.text: In the Upper Realm a pale spirit stops you on the stairs and bows deeply. "You gave back a hundred lights once," the spirit says. "Mine was one of them. I went home. I have wanted to say thank you for three hundred years."

choices.text: Ask about their home

effects.log: They tell you about a small mountain sect, an art that came back in a student's dream, a warm rain. You do not remember any of it. You listen as if it were a story about a good friend.

choices.text: Bow back, and say nothing

effects.log: You bow back. Some thanks are better received in silence. The spirit goes up the stairs, lighter. So do you.

events.text: A bandit gang has taken the pass. The villagers below have heard there is a fighter in town who "eats" bandits, and they have brought a basket of eggs as payment.

choices.text: Clear the pass

ok.log: You clear the pass. The bandits' qi rises off them like steam from a pot, and the System eats well. The villagers give you the eggs anyway.

fail.log: There are more of them than the villagers said. You come back with a cut and an apology. The villagers give you the eggs anyway. (-10 health)

choices.text: Take the eggs and send the bandits a warning

effects.log: You send a note up the pass: the Devourer is in town. By morning the bandits have gone. You eat the eggs. Some meals are better than others.

events.text: A beast core falls out of a spirit boar you scared off a farmer's field. The farmer insists you keep it.

choices.text: Keep it

effects.log: You take it home. The System hums at it all evening like a cook at a good cut.

choices.text: Give it to the farmer to sell

effects.log: "Sell it," you say. "Mend your fence." The farmer buys a new ox and names it after you, which is an honour of sorts.

events.text: The hunger is loud this year. Sitting in a teahouse, you realise you have been staring at a young martial artist at the next table, whose qi is bright and green and new.

choices.text: Leave the teahouse

effects.log: You leave your tea and walk out into the rain. The young one never knows. That is the point.

choices.text: Buy them a cup and give them advice instead

effects.log: You buy them tea and tell them three things about stances that took you decades to learn. Giving, it turns out, quiets the hunger almost as well as eating.

events.text: A wandering challenger has heard you never lose and wants to prove otherwise, at noon, in the market square.

choices.text: Accept

ok.log: You win. Their qi pours into you, bright as noon. The challenger walks away humbler and a little lighter, and writes a poem about it that becomes rather famous.

fail.log: You lose, for once. The challenger is delighted. The System is outraged. You are, privately, a little relieved that it is still possible. (-12 health)

choices.text: Decline

effects.log: You decline. The challenger calls you a coward to the whole market. You buy a melon and go home.

events.text: Heavy rain for a week. Your qi gathers like water in a cistern, and the System, bored, has started counting the raindrops on the roof.

choices.text: Meditate with the rain

effects.log: You meditate to the sound of the rain until the System loses count and falls asleep. You do not.

choices.text: Teach the System to play go

effects.log: You set up a go board and play for both sides, describing the moves aloud. The System is terrible at go. It wants to take every stone.

events.text: A sect of righteous swordsmen is preaching in the market against "devouring arts and those who practise them". You stop to listen.

choices.text: Listen to the end, and agree with half of it

effects.log: You listen to the end. Half of it is fear, and half is true. You put a coin in their bowl for the true half.

choices.text: Ask the preacher a hard question

effects.log: "And if a devourer holds back?" you ask. The preacher has no answer, and is honest enough to say so. You part on good terms.

events.text: A child in your street has a fever that will not break, and you can feel the sickness in them: a sour grey qi, clinging.

choices.text: Devour the sickness, gently

effects.log: You lay a hand on the child's forehead and draw the grey out, slowly. It tastes like a wet ash. The fever breaks by morning. You feel unwell for a week, and do not mind. (-4 health)

choices.text: Fetch the best physician in the city

effects.log: You fetch the physician and pay. The fever breaks in three days. Not everything needs a mouth. Some things need a doctor.

events.text: At a spring festival, the lanterns are lit, and the whole town's qi rises happy and loose into the night. The System sits up and sniffs the air like a dog at a kitchen door.

choices.text: Enjoy the festival like anyone else

effects.log: You eat dumplings, watch the lion dance, and lose at a game of ring toss. The System sulks. You have a wonderful night.

choices.text: Take one breath of the joy in the air

effects.log: You take one breath of the festival, light and sweet. Nobody is poorer for it. Joy, it turns out, is the one meal that grows when you share it.

events.text: Your shop of the System lists its goods as always, plainly, with prices. Tonight you catch yourself reading it the way an old miser reads an account book.

choices.text: Close the ledger and go to bed

effects.log: You close it. The hunger will be there in the morning. So will the prices.

choices.text: Plan the year's meals

effects.log: You plan: one feast in spring, one beast core at the hungry turn of autumn, nothing in winter. The System approves of planning. It has never had a plan before you.

events.text: Two drunk sect disciples pick a fight with you in an alley, not knowing who you are.

choices.text: Teach them a lesson

ok.log: You put them both in the gutter in a breath. Their qi is thin and sour with wine. The System takes it and complains about the vintage.

fail.log: One of them gets in a lucky punch. You leave them snoring in the alley with your pride a little bruised. (-6 health)

choices.text: Walk them home instead

effects.log: You take one under each arm and walk them back to their sect gate, and hand them to a very embarrassed elder. The elder sends you a jar of good wine. You give it away.

events.text: An old foe you devoured long ago, now a farmer with no qi to speak of, passes you on the road with a cart of turnips, and recognises you.

choices.text: Stop and speak to them

effects.log: You stop. They look at you a long time, and then laugh. "I grow better turnips than I ever fought," they say. You buy a sack. Neither of you mentions the qi.

choices.text: Bow, and let them pass

effects.log: You bow from the roadside. They nod, and drive on. You stand there a while after the cart is gone.

events.text: A wild spirit beast has come down from the mountain into the rice terraces, enormous and confused, trampling the young shoots.

choices.text: Drive it off by force

ok.log: You fight it in the mud of the terraces. When it falls, its wild qi floods into you, rich as a winter stew, and it limps back up the mountain smaller and calmer. The farmers cheer.

fail.log: It tosses you into a terrace pond. The farmers drive it off with drums and pots while you climb out. (-12 health)

choices.text: Lead it back up the mountain

ok.log: You walk ahead of it with a basket of turnips, calling softly, all the way up the mountain. It follows. Nobody is devoured, and the rice is saved.

fail.log: It follows you, and then it does not, and then it sits on you. The farmers have to come up with poles. (-6 health)

events.text: Your sleep is thin this year, full of the faces of the people you have devoured: not angry, only looking.

choices.text: Burn incense for them

effects.log: You burn incense at the shrine, one stick for every face you can remember. It takes all night. The faces are quieter after.

choices.text: Look back at them

effects.log: In the dream you look back at them. You do not apologise. You only look, steadily, as they do. In the morning you feel you have understood each other.

events.text: A merchant offers you a fortune for a demonstration: devour a little qi from a captured beast spirit in a cage, in front of his rich clients.

choices.text: Refuse, and open the cage

effects.log: You refuse, and on your way out you open the cage. The beast spirit goes over the wall like smoke. The merchant shouts after you for an hour.

choices.text: Refuse, and walk on

effects.log: You refuse and walk on. Your hunger is not a show. The merchant finds a juggler instead.

events.text: Spring. The rivers are high and full of melted snow-qi from the mountains, cold and clean.

choices.text: Swim upstream at dawn

effects.log: You swim against the current until the sun is up, and let the cold river qi wash through you. You come out blue and grinning and full.

choices.text: Sit on the bank and watch it go

effects.log: You sit and watch it go by. Not every river needs drinking.

events.text: A youth of the village wants to be your disciple, having heard that you can eat other people's power. "Teach me to do it," the youth says.

choices.text: Say it cannot be taught, and teach them something better

effects.log: "It cannot be taught," you say. "But this can." You teach them to breathe, to stand, to hold back. They are disappointed for a year, and grateful for the rest of their life.

choices.text: Tell them what it costs

effects.log: You tell them about the hunger, the years, the nights. They go pale. They do not ask again. You hope you have saved them something.

events.text: A sect elder you beat years ago sends a formal invitation to a rematch, "to see what the years have made of us both". The letter is polite. The handwriting is not.

choices.text: Go to the rematch

ok.log: You win again, more narrowly. Their qi comes to you, older and wiser than last time, and tastes of the years. The elder laughs on the ground. "Again in a few years," they say.

fail.log: The years have made them better than you. They help you up, very pleased with themselves, and pour you tea. You raise it to their health. (-12 health)

choices.text: Send back a gift instead

effects.log: You send a jar of good tea and a note: you won the last one. The elder writes back that this is cowardice. Then, a month later, that the tea was excellent.

events.text: In the night market an old seller of spirit beasts' cores calls you over by name, though you have never met. "The hungry one," they say. "I always keep one back for your kind."

choices.text: Buy it at the posted price (150 taels)

effects.log: You pay the price on the board. The seller wraps the core in red paper like a festival gift. Your System is very pleased.

choices.text: Ask how they knew

effects.log: "Your shadow," the seller says, "leans toward my stall." You look down. It does. You go home by a different street.

events.text: Winter. The cold seeps into your channels, and the System, sluggish, keeps asking for something warm.

choices.text: Sit by a fire and let it drink the heat

effects.log: You sit by the fire with your palms open and let the warmth soak in. It is not a meal, exactly. It is a cup of tea for a hunger.

choices.text: Train in the snow until you are warm from inside

effects.log: You train barefoot in the snow until steam rises off your shoulders. The System grumbles that this is not what it meant. (-3 health)

events.text: Your reputation has run ahead of you: in this town they bar their doors when you walk past, and a mother pulls a child indoors.

choices.text: Stop at the well and help draw water

effects.log: You stop at the well and draw water for an old man who cannot manage the rope. By evening two doors are open again. By the third day, the child is following you around.

choices.text: Walk on, and do not look back

effects.log: You walk on. Fear is a toll some roads charge. You pay it and keep going.

events.text: Two rival sects ask you to settle their quarrel by fighting each sect's champion. Both champions are young, proud and very full of qi.

choices.text: Fight both champions

ok.log: You beat them both in one afternoon. Their bright young qi comes to you in two streams. The sects, having nobody left to be proud of, make peace out of embarrassment.

fail.log: The second champion beats you. Both sects claim victory. The quarrel is worse. You leave town quickly. (-12 health)

choices.text: Make the champions spar each other while you judge

effects.log: You make them fight each other and declare it a draw. Both sects are furious with you instead of each other. It is, in its way, peace.

events.text: A traveling storyteller in the teahouse is telling the tale of the Devourer, and it is about you, and it is wrong in every detail. The audience loves it.

choices.text: Correct the storyteller afterwards

effects.log: You correct them, over tea. They take notes. The next version is more accurate and much less popular. They go back to the old one.

choices.text: Laugh along with everyone

effects.log: You laugh at your own legend with the rest of the room. In the story you devour a mountain. The System, privately, is flattered.

events.text: The Upper Realm. The air itself is qi so rich you could spoon it. Dew on the jade stairs glows. Under your ribs, where the hunger used to pace, there is only a great quiet, and even the quiet cannot decide where to begin.

choices.text: Breathe, and let it decide nothing yet

effects.log: You breathe in and out on the stairs for a whole day. The air goes into you in sips, overwhelming and kind. Nothing under your ribs answers. For once, nothing needs to.

choices.text: Drink the dew off the stairs

effects.log: You kneel and take the dew off a step. It goes into you like sunlight into water. An immortal passing raises an eyebrow. You wipe your mouth and stand up, and pretend to admire the view.

events.text: In the Upper Realm, the face in you stirs again. Since you failed to swallow it, it has been patient, and you have grown. "Again?" it asks.

choices.text: Again

ok.log: This time you are big enough. The face pours into you, the oldest hunger in the world, and at the bottom there is only a small dark thing that wanted to be full. It is yours now. You are full. The hunger answers to you.

fail.log: Not yet. You wake with a headache like a temple bell. The face in you is patient. So, you remind yourself, are you. (-14 health)

choices.text: Give it enough instead

effects.log: You give it the one thing it has not tasted since the first light: enough. Not a meal. The end of one. The System takes it, slowly, like a child taking a bowl in two hands, and goes still, and for the first time since the world began, the Maw is full. It sleeps. It will sleep forever. You feel its weight settle in you like a cat on a warm stone, and it does not wake.
